newsitem.title: UK: Iran urged to seek closer ties with Asian nations.
newsitem.headline: Iran urged to seek closer ties with Asian nations.

text.p: Iran should align itself with Asian nations rather than Europe, a leading Iranian politician said on Wednesday.

And Mohammad Javad Larijani, deputy chairman of the Iranian parliament's foreign relations committee, said there was little chance of a thaw in relations with the United States without a move from Washington.
"I believe that the United States is losing opportunities every day by not having good relations with Iran," Larijani told a news conference during a private visit to London.
"Why should we expect Iran to change its policy when there is no serious signal from Washington," he said.

Iran has rejected Western media reports linking it to the bombing of a U.S. military complex in Saudi Arabia in June that killed 19 American airmen. Some Tehran officials have said the reports showed Washington was preparing to attack Iran.
Larijani, who is also a member of Iran's National Security Council, said the Iranian reaction would be "swift and very strong" if the U.S. took action against Tehran.

He did, however, suggest that Iran and the United States had a common interest in a "collective bargain" to ensure the security of the Mideast Gulf, which he said might be turned into a demilitarised zone.
Iran has been rearming since the end of its war with Iraq in 1988 and other Gulf states have been doing the same since the end of the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait in 1991.
Asked if he felt that Iranian foreign policy was a failure because it had left Tehran isolated from the world's major super-power, Larijani said:
"If the barometer of failure is (having) relations with the United States or not, you can call it failure and we like that failure."
Washington accuses Iran of backing terrorism and seeking to obtain nuclear weapons. Tehran denies this and says the U.S. wants to destroy its Islamic government.

Larijani said Iran's relationship with Europe had become "unbalanced" and Tehran had not "exploited our Asian possibilities enough". He stressed the strength of Iran's relations with Pakistan and Turkey.
Asian countries had demonstrated competence and reliability while Iran's longstanding relationship with Europe had proved to be a "bad habit", he said.
The speaker of the Iranian parliament, Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri, had advocated an "Asian tilt", which Larijani supported.

Iran is holding presidential elections next May or June and Nateq-Nouri is seen as the leading candidate to succeed President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, who is barred from running after having served two four-year terms.
